drafted_from: tool:say-what-got-worse's own row (its words, input schema and verify sample) and the answer its command gave on that sample in this folder's test run; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Say which of today's numbers got worse than the day before", giving two readings as measures, each with label, now, before and worse_when (higher or lower). It tells you whether anything got worse, and in words which numbers moved.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes two readings as input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Say which of today's numbers got worse than the day before", and give it measures: each one a label, its now and before numbers (or lists of items), and worse_when (higher or lower).
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:say-what-got-worse and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read worse (true when any measure got worse) and said. Tell the person only when worse is true.
4. When worse is true, hand what said says to tool:tell-the-person, so the person hears it only then.

worked_examples.title: Restarts went up from 2 to 6, and one store moved most
worked_examples.ask: Say which of today's numbers got worse than the day before
worked_examples.given: The reading above: today's restarts for stores a and b, yesterday's for store a.
worked_examples.hands_back: It answered worse true, and said: "Worse than before: Restarts. Restarts: 6 (2 before); a 5 (2), b 1 (0)."
